turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hi, thanks for coming in today. What's been going on for you lately?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (sighing) Honestly? Fine, I guess — why does it matter, you probably ask everyone that. I mean, I've been okay, I guess. Just... stuff. (pausing, looking away)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's okay to not be okay. What's been hard for you lately?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looking down, tone softening slightly) It's just... people. They always seem to be pulling away, and I don't know what I'm doing wrong. Like, my roommate barely talked to me for two days and I could not stop thinking she was about to just leave, like pack up and go. (pausing, voice cracking slightly)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That must have been really difficult. Is there anything else you'd like to talk about?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (shifting in seat, tone becoming more guarded) Yeah, I don't know... nothing's really changed. I still feel... empty, I guess. Like something hollow eating a hole in me. (looking up, eyes narrowing slightly) But what's the point of talking about it, anyway?

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It can be helpful to talk through difficult feelings. Is there anything else that you would like to discuss?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (defensively) Oh, you think talking is going to fix everything? You don't get it. Nothing ever fixes. People just... they just leave, or they pretend to care, but they don't really. (crossing arms, tone becoming more confrontational) What's the point of even trying?

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It can be difficult to feel like no one cares, and I understand why you might feel that way. But it's important to remember that there are people who do care and who will listen. Is there anyone in particular you would like to talk to?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (scoffing) Oh, sure, there are people who care. They all say that at first, until they get tired of me or find someone else to focus on. (leaning forward, voice taking on a sharp tone) You're not going to be any different, are you? You're just going to sit here and listen for a few more minutes, and then you'll be off to your next appointment, and I'll be left with nothing.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I'm sorry you feel that way. Is there anything else you would like to discuss?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (getting up from the couch, tone abrupt) No, I think that's enough for today. I'm just... tired of talking. (starting to walk towards the door)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Is there anything else I can do to help?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (stopping at the door, turning back with a hint of accusation) Yeah, you can just... be honest with me. Tell me if you're bored or if you think I'm wasting your time. Don't just sit there being nice and pretend like this is helping. (eyes narrowing) I can tell when people are just going through the motions.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I'm committed to helping you in whatever way works best for you. Is there anything else I can do to help?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looking away, tone softening slightly) No... I don't know. Just... just don't promise me something you can't deliver, okay? (pausing, then turning to leave again) I'm done for today.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Alright. Let's take a break for today, and we can continue next time. Is that okay?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (nodding, but still looking away) Yeah, okay. Whatever.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: All right, see you next time.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (short, sharp nod, then quickly exiting the room)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: (standing, watching Human leave)
